title: Playback validator for billing replay and surface discrepancies
creator: Asha Patel
description: Build a replay-based validator that consumes captured request/response traces and replays them through a deterministic simulator to verify that on-chain ledger entries (internal billing ledgers) match expected token counts and quota debits. The tool must handle fragmented streaming frames, out-of-order arrival, mid-stream model switches, and partial-client reconnects. It will be used by billing engineering, SRE, and finance to detect recurring gaps and provide forensic artifacts for dispute investigations.
acceptance_criteria: Replay engine can rehydrate traces from the golden capture store (S3) and play them deterministically into the simulator with tokenization controlled by a pinned tokenizer binary.
Per-session delta report produced: expected_token_debits vs ledger_token_debits with checksum and byte-offset mapping for each fragment.
Supports streaming edge cases: truncated frames, reconnects, mid-stream model fallback; validator reproduces how production billing pipeline would attribute prefix tokens and final output credits.
Discrepancy classification rules implemented (e.g., tokenizer drift, partial-finalization, duplicate frames, clock skew) and surfaced as human-readable root causes.
Integration tests cover 300 synthetic scenarios including rare interleavings; false-positive rate on staging < 0.5%.
Dashboard and alerting tile created in Console showing daily replay mismatch rate and top offending trace signatures.
tech_notes: Implementation plan: Go service 'billing-replay' that uses existing trace ingestion API. Deterministic tokenization via locked tok-v2 binary; tokenizer version embedded in trace metadata. Replayer will offer two modes: dry-run (no ledger write) and assert mode (compare to ledger snapshot). Use session-anchor timestamps to normalize clock skew and map WS frame sequence numbers to token offsets. Idempotency mapping required for deduped frames: maintain ephemeral mapping table during replay. Store replay artifacts in S3 under 'replay-artifacts/{date}/{trace-id}'. Access controls: traces are PII-sanitized and encrypted with KMS; only billing-engineering role can read. Performance: capable of 200 replays/hour on a small staging fleet; parallelize by tenant. We'll add a lightweight checksum (sha256 of normalized fragment payloads) to speed-match traces to ledger entries.
testing_plan: Unit tests around deterministic tokenizer bindings and fragment-to-token offset mapping.
Integration: replay 10k historical traces from last 7 days on staging and compute mismatch histogram.
Synthetic scenarios: fuzz WS fragmentation, inject duplicate frames, simulate model fallback mid-stream, and ensure classification logic matches expected root cause.
Run a controlled backfill: select 500 invoices with customer disputes and verify whether replay identifies root cause.
CI gate: PR must include an end-to-end test that replays 50 small traces and validates reports are produced.
